sessions.title: CONTEXT / GOAL: Implement EPMEDUAI-1315 for the ToDoApplication repo (surajsalunkhe/ToDoApplication). Currently TodoJpaResource (restful-web-services/src/main/java/com/todoapp/rest/webservices/restfulwebservices/todo/TodoJpaResource.java) exposes /jpa/users/{username}/todos endpoints that trust the {username} path param and the request body's username field without verifying they match the authenticated principal, and GET/PUT/DELETE by {id} do not check that the todo belongs to the path/authenticated user. This is an IDOR vulnerability: user 'alice' can read/modify/delete user 'bob' todos by changing the URL. Implement server-side ownership enforcement so a user can only read/write their own todos, using the authenticated principal (from Spring Security's SecurityContextHolder) as the source of truth, never the path or request body. BACKEND CHANGES (restful-web-services): 1. Entity (Todo.java) — no field changes required. Existing username field is sufficient for ownership checks. 2. Repository (TodoJpaRepository.java): - Add: Optional findByIdAndUsername(Long id, String username) - Add: void deleteByIdAndUsername(Long id, String username) if used directly, otherwise implement find-then-delete in the service layer. - Keep existing findByUsername(String username) for the list endpoint. 3. New Service layer — create a TodoOwnershipService (or extend/introduce a TodoService with user-scoped operations) in the todo package: - assertSameUser(pathUsername, authenticatedUsername): throws an authorization exception (mapped to 403) when they differ. - getOwnedTodoOrThrow(id, authenticatedUsername): loads via findByIdAndUsername; throws an authorization/not-found exception when no match is found (belongs to another user or doesn't exist). - listTodosForUser(pathUsername, authenticatedUsername): validates ownership, then returns todos for the authenticated user. - createTodoForUser(pathUsername, todo, authenticatedUsername): validates path/username match, forces todo.username = authenticatedUsername (ignore any username in the request body), saves and returns created todo. - updateTodoForUser(pathUsername, id, todo, authenticatedUsername): validates ownership of the existing todo (must belong to authenticatedUsername), forces todo.id = id and todo.username = authenticatedUsername before saving. - deleteTodoForUser(pathUsername, id, authenticatedUsername): validates ownership before deleting; no-op/error if the todo doesn't belong to the authenticated user. 4. Controller (TodoJpaResource.java) — update all five endpoints: - GET /jpa/users/{username}/todos: retrieve authenticated username via SecurityContextHolder.getContext().getAuthentication().getName(); if it does not equal the path {username}, return 403 Forbidden and do not query/return any data. Otherwise return only that user's todos. - GET /jpa/users/{username}/todos/{id}: enforce same-user check on the path; then look up the todo via findByIdAndUsername(id, authenticatedUsername) (not findById alone). If the todo does not belong to the authenticated user (or path check fails), return 403 Forbidden and do not leak whether the todo exists or belongs to someone else. - POST /jpa/users/{username}/todos: enforce same-user check on the path; ignore/override any username field present in the request body — the server must set todo.username to the authenticated principal, not the path value or body value, before persisting. - PUT /jpa/users/{username}/todos/{id}: enforce same-user check on the path; verify the todo with {id} currently belongs to the authenticated user (403 if not, including if it belongs to another user); force todo.setId(id) and todo.setUsername(authenticatedUsername) before saving so the update cannot move/reassign ownership. - DELETE /jpa/users/{username}/todos/{id}: enforce same-user check on the path; verify the todo with {id} belongs to the authenticated user before deleting; return 403 Forbidden and do not delete if ownership check fails. - Replace direct todoJpaRepository calls in the controller with calls into the new service/ownership layer described above. 5. Validation and error handling: - Introduce (or reuse if present) an exception type representing "access denied" and map it via @ControllerAdvice / @ExceptionHandler (or ResponseStatusException) to HTTP 403 Forbidden with a minimal, non-leaking error body (do not reveal whether the resource exists under another user). - Ensure no stack traces or internal details are returned in the 403 response body. - This design adopts 403 Forbidden (not 404) for all ownership-violation cases, per the LLD decision. 6. Security configuration impact (JWTWebSecurityConfig.java, restful-web-services/src/main/java/com/todoapp/rest/webservices/restfulwebservices/jwt/): - No new roles are required (single-role "user can access own todos" model, no RBAC expansion). - Confirm that all /jpa/users/** endpoints remain behind .anyRequest().authenticated() (already the case) so SecurityContextHolder always has a valid principal before controller methods execute. - No CORS changes are required, but confirm @CrossOrigin origin on TodoJpaResource stays consistent with the frontend PWA's origin. 7. Likely files to touch: - restful-web-services/src/main/java/com/todoapp/rest/webservices/restfulwebservices/todo/TodoJpaResource.java - restful-web-services/src/main/java/com/todoapp/rest/webservices/restfulwebservices/todo/TodoJpaRepository.java - restful-web-services/src/main/java/com/todoapp/rest/webservices/restfulwebservices/todo/Todo.java (only if adding indexes via annotations) - New: restful-web-services/src/main/java/com/todoapp/rest/webservices/restfulwebservices/todo/TodoOwnershipService.java (or TodoService.java) - New: an exception class + a @ControllerAdvice/exception handler for 403 mapping (place under an existing exceptions/errorhandling package if one exists, otherwise create restful-web-services/src/main/java/com/todoapp/rest/webservices/restfulwebservices/todo/exception or similar consistent with existing project conventions). FRONTEND CHANGES (frontend/todo-app-pwa): 1. Axios/service layer (src/api/todo/TodoDataService.js): - No signature changes are required to retrieveAllTodos(name), retrieveTodo(name, id), deleteTodo(name, id), updateTodo(name, id, todo), createTodo(name, todo) — they already pass the current logged-in username via callers. - Add centralized handling for HTTP 403 responses returned by these calls (e.g., via an axios response interceptor or per-call .catch blocks) so any ownership-violation response is surfaced to the UI rather than causing an unhandled promise rejection. 2. Components: - src/components/todoList.js: in refreshTodos, deleteTodoCLicked (and any future update triggers), add error handling for 403 responses — set an error/message state (reuse existing message state or add an error state) and render a Material UI Alert/Snackbar (or existing message div, following existing UI pattern) such as "Not allowed" when the API returns 403, instead of silently failing. - src/components/todo.js: in the useEffect retrieveTodo call and the onSubmit create/update calls, add 403 handling — display an inline error message (Material UI text or Alert consistent with existing style) and avoid navigating to /todo on failure (only navigate on success as today). - Ensure the username value sent from the frontend for createTodo/updateTodo bodies continues to be the logged-in username (AuthenticationService.getLoggedInUserName()), understanding that the backend will now authoritatively enforce/overwrite it regardless of what is sent. 3. State/UI behaviors to add: - Loading state: no new loading indicators are required beyond what exists, unless the LLD/story implies otherwise (it does not) — keep existing patterns. - Error state: add a visible, user-facing error message for 403 Forbidden responses on list/get/create/update/delete calls, using Material UI components already used in the app (Button/TableCell text or a simple styled div, consistent with the existing message pattern in todoList.js). - Empty state: no change required. ACCEPANCE CRITERIA (from Jira story, testable): 1. Given a user authenticated as "alice", when calling GET /jpa/users/bob/todos, then the API returns 403 Forbidden and does not return bob's data. 2. Given a user authenticated as "alice" and a todo {id} that belongs to "bob", when calling PUT /jpa/users/alice/todos/{id} or DELETE /jpa/users/alice/todos/{id}, then the API returns 403 Forbidden and does not modify or delete the todo. 3. Given a user authenticated as "alice" and a todo {id} that belongs to "bob", when calling GET /jpa/users/alice/todos/{id}, then the API returns 403 Forbidden and does not return bob's todo data. 4. Given a user creates a todo via POST /jpa/users/alice/todos while authenticated as "alice", when the JSON body includes a different username value, then the server persists the todo under "alice" (server-controlled ownership), ignoring the body's username. 5. Given a user authenticated as "alice" calling any /jpa/users/alice/todos... endpoint (matching path/principal, and for id-based operations, owning the resource), then the request succeeds exactly as before (no regression for legitimate same-user access). 6. No stack trace or internal error detail is exposed in any 403 response body. TESTING NOTES: - Backend unit tests (JUnit, add under restful-web-services/src/test/java/com/todoapp/rest/webservices
